md_description: This DAG represents a freshwater lake microbial ecology workflow spanning multiple lakes, depths, zones, and seasons. It covers collection and processing of water samples, environmental measurements of temperature, dissolved oxygen, and nutrients, and 18S rRNA marker-gene sequencing of eukaryotic microbial communities. The workflow produces raw sequencing signals, processed abundance and taxonomy derivatives, a curated metadata table, and an integrated analysis dataset for studying environmental gradients and seasonal dynamics in freshwater ecosystems.

freshwater_lake_water_sample.reasoning: This node is an Entity, so I included only intrinsic identity/origin fields for the discrete water sample and excluded any process, capture, signal, or derivative details. The sample’s semantic territory is the sampled unit itself: which lake it came from, where and when it was collected, and what it represents as a physical specimen. I avoided fields already generated elsewhere in the DAG such as environmental measurements, sequencing outputs, metadata table contents, or downstream analysis fields. Because sample identifiers are generated once at the root Entity level, I included a single sample identifier field and then origin/context fields needed to distinguish samples across lakes, depths, zones, dates, and seasons.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the discrete lake water sample; use a stable string format such as 'L01_D05_PEL_2024-06-12' or a project-specific alphanumeric code. This identifier is assigned at collection time and is the primary key used to link the sample to downstream filtration, chemistry, sequencing, and metadata records.

Name of the freshwater lake where the sample was collected, recorded at sampling time from the source water body. Use the standardized project lake label, for example 'Lake_A' or the official lake name.

Depth of water column from which the sample was taken, measured in meters at the time of collection. Typical range is 0 to the maximum lake depth sampled in the study; record as a numeric value such as 0.5, 5.0, or 12.3.
Lake zone or habitat compartment where the sample was collected, recorded during field sampling. Use a controlled category to distinguish spatial sampling strata within each lake.

Date on which the water sample was collected, recorded at the moment of field sampling in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD), for example '2024-06-12'. This anchors seasonal comparisons across lakes and sampling campaigns.
Season assigned to the sampling date for ecological comparison across repeated campaigns. Use a project-defined categorical season label derived from the collection date and regional phenology.
Material type represented by the entity; for this node it should always indicate lake water. This distinguishes water samples from biomass, DNA extracts, libraries, or derived data products.

water_filtering.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I included only protocol and operation details for the filtration step itself: how the water was filtered to concentrate microbial biomass. I excluded sample identity/origin fields because those belong to the upstream water sample entity, and I excluded downstream properties such as retained biomass composition or filter-derived artifacts because those belong to the output entity. I also avoided any fields already generated for the sample entity or other workflow nodes, and focused on reproducible process parameters, filter hardware, and a simple process-quality indicator needed to interpret the filtration step.

md_schema.descr: Operational filtration approach used to concentrate microbial biomass from the lake water sample at the collection site or in the field lab. Record the method name as a controlled category such as vacuum filtration or pressure filtration.

Nominal pore size of the filter used during water filtration, measured or specified by the manufacturer in micrometers. Typical values for microbial biomass capture are 0.2, 0.45, or 1.0 micrometers; record the value used for the sample.

Total volume of lake water passed through the filter during this process step, measured in liters at the time of filtration. Typical range is project-dependent and may be sub-liter to several liters per sample, depending on biomass concentration and clogging.

Elapsed time required to complete filtration for the sample, measured in minutes from start to finish of the water filtering operation. Use this to document process efficiency and any clogging-related delays.
Primary material of the filter membrane or capture device used to retain microbial biomass. Record as a controlled category to support reproducibility and downstream DNA extraction compatibility.

Manufacturer model or device name of the filtration apparatus used for the process, recorded as the actively used hardware configuration. Example: a specific vacuum manifold or pump model used during filtration.

Simple process quality indicator stating whether the water filtration step completed successfully and produced retained biomass suitable for downstream DNA extraction. Record true when filtration was completed without major sample loss; false when the step failed or was aborted.

filtered_biomass.reasoning: This node is an Entity, so I included only intrinsic properties of the retained biomass itself and excluded filtration protocol details, sample origin, DNA extraction conditions, and downstream sequencing products. The key descriptive territory here is what the biomass is after concentration: the filter type it is associated with, whether the retained material is sufficient for downstream extraction, how it was stored, and its physical appearance/quantity proxy. I avoided reusing the upstream filtration process fields and avoided any downstream DNA or library metrics. I also avoided fields already generated for the original water sample entity except where needed to describe the biomass as a specimen derived from that sample.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the filtered biomass specimen retained on the filter after concentrating a lake water sample. Use a stable string format such as 'FB_L01_D05_2024-06-12_01' or the project-specific barcode used to track the retained material through DNA extraction.

Nominal pore size of the filter on which the biomass was retained, recorded in micrometers to describe the physical capture context of the specimen. Typical values are 0.2, 0.45, or 1.0 micrometers, matching the filtration step used upstream.

Temperature at which the retained biomass was stored after filtration and before DNA extraction, measured in degrees Celsius. Record the storage condition at the time the specimen is archived, for example -20, -80, or 4.

Time elapsed between filtration and the start of DNA extraction for this retained biomass, measured in hours. Typical range may be from less than 1 hour to several days depending on field logistics and freezing conditions.
Method used to preserve the retained biomass on the filter prior to DNA extraction. Record the preservation approach as a controlled category to support comparison across samples.

Approximate visual assessment of the amount of retained biomass on the filter after water concentration, recorded as a categorical or ordinal field to indicate whether capture was sparse or abundant. Use the project’s standardized scoring system if available at specimen inspection.

dna_extraction.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I included only DNA extraction protocol details and extraction performance for the operation itself. I excluded upstream filtered biomass identity and preservation fields, and I excluded downstream extracted DNA properties such as concentration or purity because those belong to the output entity. I also avoided duplicating sample or biomass identifiers already generated earlier. The fields focus on extraction chemistry, kit/instrument configuration, elution conditions, and a simple success/yield indicator needed to reproduce and evaluate the extraction step.

md_schema.descr: Commercial kit or in-house extraction chemistry used to isolate nucleic acids from the filtered biomass during this process step. Record the kit name or method designation used for the sample, for example a bead-beating soil/microbial DNA kit.

Protocol or standard operating procedure version applied during DNA extraction, recorded as a version string so the exact workflow can be reproduced. Example formats include 'v1.0', '2024-03', or a lab SOP identifier.

Final elution volume used to recover purified DNA from the extraction column or beads, measured in microliters at the end of the extraction step. Typical values may range from 30 to 100 microliters depending on the kit and laboratory protocol.
Total elapsed time required to complete DNA extraction for the sample, measured in minutes from lysis start to eluate recovery. Use this to capture protocol efficiency and batch-to-batch variation.

Manufacturer model or device used during the extraction process when active hardware is part of the workflow, such as a bead beater, homogenizer, or automated extractor. Record the specific instrument model used for the sample.

Process outcome indicating whether the DNA extraction step completed successfully and produced an extract suitable for downstream amplicon library preparation. Record true if an extract was obtained without major contamination or failure; false otherwise.

extracted_dna.reasoning: This node is an Entity, so I included only intrinsic properties of the purified DNA extract itself and excluded extraction protocol settings, filtered biomass properties, and downstream library or sequencing details. The most useful fields here are identity/tracking, quantity, quality, and storage conditions of the DNA material after extraction. I avoided duplicating process fields such as kit, elution volume, or duration, and I did not include output-specific sequencing metrics. The fields are limited to what downstream users need to assess whether the DNA extract is suitable for amplicon library preparation and to link it through the workflow.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the purified community DNA extract obtained from filtered biomass. Use a stable project-specific string such as 'DNA_L01_D05_2024-06-12_A' or a barcode linked to the extract tube.

Measured concentration of the purified DNA extract at the time it is assessed for downstream library preparation, reported in nanograms per microliter. Typical values for environmental extracts may range from below 1 to tens of ng/µL depending on biomass yield.

Total amount of DNA recovered in the final extract, reported in nanograms and calculated from concentration multiplied by elution volume when available. Record the value at the time of extract QC or library input assessment.

Spectrophotometric purity ratio A260/A280 measured for the purified DNA extract at QC time. Typical values near 1.8 indicate relatively pure DNA; values substantially lower or higher may indicate contamination or assay issues.

Qualitative assessment of the physical integrity of the DNA extract at QC time, used to judge whether the extract is suitable for amplicon library preparation. Record as a controlled category based on lab assessment.
Temperature at which the purified DNA extract is stored after extraction and before downstream library preparation, measured in degrees Celsius. Common storage conditions include 4, -20, or -80.
Identifier for the extraction batch in which this DNA extract was produced, useful for linking multiple extracts processed together. Use a stable string format such as 'EXT_BATCH_2024_06_01'.

amplicon_library_prep.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I included only the library preparation parameters and performance characteristics of the amplification/indexing operation itself. I excluded upstream DNA extract properties and downstream library properties such as fragment distribution or sequencing file outputs, because those belong to the input or output entities. I also avoided repeating process fields already used for DNA extraction or sequencing capture. The fields focus on primer/index choices, PCR cycling conditions, polymerase chemistry, input DNA amount, and whether the library was successfully prepared for sequencing, which are the minimum reproducibility details for this step.

md_schema.descr: Marker-gene region amplified during library preparation for this freshwater 18S survey. Record the targeted amplicon region used for eukaryotic community profiling, for example the 18S rRNA gene variable region selected by the project.
Forward primer nucleotide sequence used to amplify the 18S marker region during library preparation. Record the exact oligonucleotide sequence in 5' to 3' orientation as used in the PCR reaction.
Reverse primer nucleotide sequence used to amplify the 18S marker region during library preparation. Record the exact oligonucleotide sequence in 5' to 3' orientation as used in the PCR reaction.

Number of PCR amplification cycles applied during amplicon library preparation. Typical marker-gene library prep uses a moderate cycle count such as 20 to 35 cycles, depending on input DNA quantity and assay design.

Annealing temperature used in the PCR program for library amplification, measured in degrees Celsius. Record the temperature used in the thermal cycling protocol, commonly within a mid-range suitable for the primer set.

Amount of purified DNA input into the amplicon library preparation reaction, measured in nanograms at the time of PCR setup. Typical values may range from sub-nanogram to tens of nanograms depending on sample yield and assay sensitivity.
Library indexing approach used to add sample-specific identifiers during amplification or clean-up, recorded as a controlled category. This supports multiplexing in sequencing.

Outcome of the amplicon library preparation process, indicating whether the 18S library was successfully amplified, indexed, and made suitable for sequencing. Record true if the library passed basic preparation checks; false otherwise.

eukaryotic_amplicon_library.reasoning: This node is an Entity, so I included only intrinsic properties of the prepared 18S amplicon library and excluded PCR conditions, primer sequences, and sequencing run settings because those belong to the upstream preparation process or downstream sequencing capture. The most useful library-level fields are identity, indexed status, concentration/size metrics, and storage conditions, which help determine whether the library is ready for sequencing and how it should be tracked. I avoided duplicating process fields already generated for amplicon library prep and did not include raw-read or instrument configuration fields.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the indexed 18S amplicon library prepared from extracted community DNA. Use a stable project-specific string such as 'LIB_L01_D05_2024-06-12_A' or a tube/barcode identifier linked to the sequencing submission.

Indicator that the library contains sample-specific index sequences for multiplexed sequencing. This is an intrinsic property of the prepared library and should reflect whether indexing adapters were successfully incorporated.

Measured concentration of the prepared amplicon library at QC or submission time, reported in nanograms per microliter. Typical values may range from below 1 to tens of ng/µL depending on amplification success and cleanup efficiency.

Representative fragment size of the prepared amplicon library, measured in base pairs by electrophoresis or capillary analysis at QC time. For 18S amplicons, typical sizes depend on the targeted region and primer set and should reflect the dominant library peak.

Qualitative assessment of whether the prepared library passed pre-sequencing QC and is suitable for loading onto the sequencer. Record a controlled category based on laboratory review of concentration, size, and cleanliness.
Temperature at which the prepared 18S library is stored before sequencing, measured in degrees Celsius. Common storage conditions include 4, -20, or -80 depending on turnaround time.
Identifier for the batch or plate submission in which the library was grouped for sequencing. Use a stable string format such as 'SEQ_SUB_2024_06_01' to track multiplexed handoff.

field_temperature_measurement.reasoning: This node is a Capture, so I included only the measurement session and instrument configuration for the temperature reading itself. I excluded sample identity, depth/zone context, and the resulting raw temperature record because those belong to the upstream sample entity and downstream signal node, respectively. Per the rules, capture nodes should describe the actively configured hardware, calibration, and reading conditions of the instrument. I therefore focused on the sonde configuration, probe calibration, measurement timing, and operator-controlled settings needed to reproduce the temperature capture without duplicating environmental or file-level information.

md_schema.descr: Manufacturer of the field temperature probe or multiparameter sonde used to measure water temperature during sampling. Record the hardware vendor name for the instrument actively configured in this capture session.

Model designation of the field temperature probe or sonde used for the temperature measurement, recorded as part of the instrument configuration. Example: a specific multiparameter sonde model used in lake fieldwork.
Serial number of the instrument used for the temperature capture session, recorded to uniquely identify the deployed probe. Use the manufacturer-issued serial string exactly as printed on the device.

Date on which the temperature probe was last calibrated or verified before the capture session, recorded in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD). This provides traceability for the measurement session and instrument accuracy.

Operational mode used to obtain the water temperature reading, such as spot measurement, averaged reading, or continuous logging during the capture session. Use a controlled category that reflects how the instrument was configured at sampling time.

Number of repeated temperature readings taken at the sampling point during this capture session before recording the final value. Typical counts are 1 for spot capture or multiple readings when averaging is used.

Indicator that the temperature measurement session produced a valid reading at the intended sampling depth and zone. Record true when the probe returned an acceptable value and false when the session failed or was invalidated.

water_temperature_signal.reasoning: This node is a Signal, so I included only raw data artefact properties: the recorded temperature value, its units, technical readout characteristics, and storage/file-level metadata for the measurement record. I excluded probe manufacturer/model/calibration details because those belong to the upstream Capture node, and I excluded sample lake/depth/zone context because those belong to the Entity node. I also avoided any scientific interpretation or environmental summary fields. The goal is to capture what the raw temperature record is technically, where it is stored, and whether the record appears complete and valid as a signal artifact.

md_schema.descr: Raw temperature value recorded by the field probe for the sampled lake location during the measurement event, reported in degrees Celsius. This is the primary numerical observation captured at the sampling depth and zone; typical freshwater lake values may range from near 0 to around 30 degrees Celsius depending on season and geography.

Reported precision or resolution of the raw temperature record, in degrees Celsius, as provided by the instrument or data logger. Use this to document the technical granularity of the captured signal, such as 0.01 or 0.1 degrees Celsius.

Technical quality flag associated with the raw temperature record, indicating whether the signal was accepted, flagged, or rejected during data ingestion. Use a controlled category to reflect the integrity of the raw artifact rather than the environmental condition itself.

Timestamp associated with the raw temperature record as stored in the signal artifact, recorded in ISO 8601 format (date-time). Use this to preserve the exact acquisition time when available from the data logger.

File or record format used to store the raw temperature signal, such as CSV, TSV, JSON, or instrument-exported text. This describes the technical packaging of the raw measurement artifact rather than the scientific content.
Size of the raw temperature signal file or record bundle, measured in bytes at the time of storage or export. This helps track the technical scale of the artifact and verify completeness.

dissolved_oxygen_measurement.reasoning: This node is a Capture, so I included only the dissolved oxygen measurement session and instrument configuration, not the raw oxygen value or the sample’s lake/depth/zone identity. Those raw readings belong on the downstream Signal node, while sample provenance stays on the Entity node. Per the capture rules, the important metadata here are the hardware manufacturer/model/serial number, calibration state, operating mode, and any measurement settings controlled during the field probe session. I kept the schema focused on reproducible instrument configuration and whether the oxygen reading session succeeded.

md_schema.descr: Manufacturer of the dissolved oxygen probe or multiparameter sonde used during the field measurement session. Record the hardware vendor for the actively configured instrument.
Model designation of the dissolved oxygen probe or sonde used to measure oxygen at the sampling point. Record the specific instrument model used in the capture session.
Serial number of the dissolved oxygen instrument used for this measurement session, recorded to uniquely identify the deployed probe. Use the manufacturer-issued serial identifier.
Date on which the dissolved oxygen probe was last calibrated or verified before the capture session, recorded in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD). This provides traceability for measurement accuracy.
Operational mode used to capture dissolved oxygen, such as spot reading, averaged reading, or logged measurement. Use a controlled category reflecting how the probe was configured during sampling.

Indicator of whether the probe applied compensation settings during the measurement session, such as temperature or barometric compensation. This documents actively configured capture behavior that can affect the reading.

Indicator that the dissolved oxygen measurement session produced a valid reading at the intended sampling depth and zone. Record true when the probe returned an acceptable value and false when the session failed or was invalidated.

dissolved_oxygen_signal.reasoning: This node is a Signal, so I included only raw dissolved oxygen record properties: the measured oxygen value, its units, technical precision, and file/record metadata. I excluded probe configuration and calibration details because those belong to the upstream Capture node, and I excluded sample provenance or ecological interpretation because those belong elsewhere in the DAG. The schema is limited to the raw artifact and its technical validity so downstream users can inspect the measurement without conflating it with instrument settings or environmental context.

md_schema.descr: Raw dissolved oxygen value recorded by the field probe for the sampled lake location during the measurement event, reported in milligrams per liter. Typical freshwater values may range from near 0 to saturation levels that vary with temperature and altitude.

Reported precision or resolution of the raw dissolved oxygen record, in milligrams per liter, as provided by the instrument or logger. Use this to document the technical granularity of the captured signal, such as 0.01 or 0.1 mg/L.

Technical quality flag associated with the raw dissolved oxygen record, indicating whether the signal was accepted, flagged, or rejected during ingestion. Use a controlled category to reflect artifact integrity rather than ecological condition.

Timestamp associated with the raw dissolved oxygen record as stored in the signal artifact, recorded in ISO 8601 format (date-time). Use this to preserve the exact acquisition time when available from the data logger.

File or record format used to store the raw dissolved oxygen signal, such as CSV, TSV, JSON, or instrument-exported text. This describes the technical packaging of the raw measurement artifact rather than the scientific content.
Size of the raw dissolved oxygen signal file or record bundle, measured in bytes at the time of storage or export. This helps track the technical scale of the artifact and verify completeness.

nutrient_assay_measurement.reasoning: This node is a Capture, so I included only the assay session and instrument configuration for the nutrient measurement operation. I excluded the sample’s lake/depth/zone identity and the raw concentration records, because those belong to the upstream Entity and downstream Signal nodes. Per the capture rules, the important information is the analytical platform, calibration, assay mode, and any operator-controlled settings that determine how nutrient concentrations were measured from the water sample. I also kept the schema general enough to support the likely multi-analyte chemistry assay used in this freshwater workflow.

md_schema.descr: Manufacturer of the water chemistry analyzer or assay platform used to measure nutrient concentrations from the lake water sample. Record the hardware vendor for the actively configured analytical instrument.
Model designation of the chemistry analyzer used for the nutrient assay, recorded as part of the capture session configuration. Example: a specific bench-top or field chemistry platform model.
Serial number of the analytical instrument used for the nutrient measurement session, recorded to uniquely identify the device. Use the manufacturer-issued serial identifier.

Analytical method or assay chemistry used to quantify nutrients in the sampled water, recorded as a controlled category describing the capture mode. Use the method that best matches the lab workflow for nutrient analysis.
Date on which the nutrient analyzer was last calibrated or verified before the capture session, recorded in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD). This provides traceability for measurement accuracy.

List or designation of nutrient analytes targeted by the assay session, such as nitrate, nitrite, ammonium, phosphate, or total nitrogen/phosphorus. Record the panel name or assay scope used for the sample.
Indicator that the nutrient assay session produced valid measurements for the sampled water. Record true when the assay completed successfully and false when the session failed or was invalidated.

nutrient_concentration_signal.reasoning: This node is a Signal, so I included only raw assay output properties: the measured nutrient values, their units, technical quality, and file/record metadata. I excluded analyzer manufacturer/model/calibration and assay-method details because those belong to the upstream Capture node, and I excluded sample provenance because that belongs to the Entity node. Since the nutrient step may involve multiple analytes, I focused on a raw artifact structure that can hold individual nutrient measurements and preserve the technical packaging of the record without interpretation.

md_schema.descr: Name of the nutrient analyte reported in the raw assay record, such as nitrate, nitrite, ammonium, phosphate, total nitrogen, or total phosphorus. Use one row or record per analyte when the assay returns a panel of measurements.

Raw concentration value for the nutrient analyte in the sampled lake water, reported in milligrams per liter unless the assay uses another standard unit. Typical freshwater values are analyte-dependent and may span orders of magnitude.
Unit associated with the raw nutrient concentration value as stored in the signal artifact, such as mg/L, µg/L, or mmol/L. Record the exact unit used in the exported measurement record.
Reported precision or resolution of the raw nutrient measurement, in the same unit system used for the analyte record. Use this to document the technical granularity of the signal, such as 0.01 mg/L.

Technical quality flag associated with the raw nutrient measurement record, indicating whether the signal was accepted, flagged, or rejected during ingestion. Use a controlled category to reflect artifact integrity rather than environmental interpretation.

Timestamp associated with the raw nutrient record as stored in the signal artifact, recorded in ISO 8601 format (date-time). Use this to preserve the exact acquisition or export time when available from the instrument or logger.

File or record format used to store the raw nutrient signal, such as CSV, TSV, JSON, or instrument-exported text. This describes the technical packaging of the raw measurement artifact rather than the scientific content.
Size of the raw nutrient signal file or record bundle, measured in bytes at the time of storage or export. This helps track the technical scale of the artifact and verify completeness.

sequencing_capture.reasoning: This node is a Capture, so I included only the sequencing run session and instrument configuration for generating the raw reads. I excluded library identity and quality because those belong to the upstream amplicon library entity, and I excluded FASTQ/file properties because those belong to the downstream raw signal node. Per the capture rules, the relevant metadata are the sequencer manufacturer/model/serial, run chemistry, read length settings, and run success, which together describe how the instrument was configured to read the 18S library.

md_schema.descr: Manufacturer of the sequencing instrument used to read the prepared 18S amplicon library. Record the hardware vendor for the actively configured sequencer in this capture session.
Model designation of the sequencer used for the marker-gene run, recorded as part of the instrument configuration. Example: a specific Illumina platform model used for the capture session.
Serial number of the sequencing instrument used for this run, recorded to uniquely identify the device. Use the manufacturer-issued serial string exactly as tracked in the instrument logs.
Sequencing chemistry or reagent kit version used for the run, recorded as the actively configured chemistry for the capture session. This helps reproduce base-calling behavior and read quality.

Configured number of sequencing cycles used to generate forward and reverse reads for the 18S amplicon library, measured as total cycles or per-read cycle counts depending on run setup. Typical values depend on the amplicon length and platform configuration.

Run mode used during sequencing, such as single-end or paired-end, recorded as a controlled category for the capture session. Use the mode that matches how the instrument was configured for this library.
Date on which the sequencing capture session was initiated or completed, recorded in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD). This anchors the raw-read generation event in time.
Indicator that the sequencing run produced valid raw reads from the prepared library. Record true when the run completed and yielded usable signal; false when the session failed or was invalidated.

raw_fastq_reads.reasoning: This node is a Signal, so I included only technical properties of the raw FASTQ artefact: file format, file size, read count, read length, compression, and a simple technical quality flag. I excluded sequencer manufacturer/model/chemistry because those belong to the upstream Capture node, and I excluded any biological interpretation or processed-read metrics because those belong to downstream process or derivative nodes. The intent is to describe the raw sequencing file itself so users can assess completeness, storage, and technical suitability before processing.

md_schema.descr: Technical file format used for the raw sequencing reads, typically FASTQ or an instrument-exported FASTQ variant. Record the container/format of the raw read artifact as stored after sequencing capture.
Total size of the raw FASTQ file or file bundle, measured in bytes at the time of storage or transfer. This supports integrity checks and storage tracking for the sequencing signal artifact.
Number of reads contained in the raw FASTQ artifact, counted at the point of file export or ingestion. Typical values depend on sequencing depth and multiplexing strategy.
Nominal length of reads in the raw FASTQ file, measured in base pairs. For paired-end data, record the per-read cycle length or the read length represented in the file bundle.
Indicator of whether the raw FASTQ artifact is compressed for storage or transfer. Record true if gzip or equivalent compression was applied; false if the file is plain text FASTQ.

Technical quality flag associated with the raw FASTQ artifact, indicating whether the file was accepted, flagged, or rejected during ingestion. Use this to represent file-level integrity rather than biological quality.

basecalling_demultiplexing.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I included only the processing parameters and software configuration for separating raw sequencing reads into per-sample files. I excluded the raw FASTQ file properties because those belong to the upstream Signal node, and I excluded the demultiplexed read file properties because those belong to the downstream Signal node. Per the rules, process nodes should describe the software used, version, key settings, barcode behavior, and success of the conversion step, not the resulting file artifacts themselves. I therefore focused on the demultiplexing workflow run configuration needed to reproduce this read-processing step.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software or pipeline used to basecall and demultiplex raw sequencing reads into per-sample files. Record the package or workflow name that actively processed the reads in this step.

Version of the basecalling/demultiplexing software used for the processing step, recorded as a version string such as 'v2024.5' or a semantic version. This is required to reproduce read processing behavior.
Maximum number of barcode mismatches allowed during demultiplexing, measured as an integer count of allowed base differences. This parameter controls how stringently reads are assigned to samples.

Minimum quality threshold applied during read conversion and sample assignment, expressed as the platform’s configured cutoff value. Record the threshold used to accept or discard reads during processing.

Identifier or path-like reference to the processing log generated by the demultiplexing run, used for traceability of this step. This is a process-level record of execution rather than a read file artifact.

Indicator that the basecalling and demultiplexing step completed successfully and produced per-sample read files suitable for downstream denoising. Record true when processing finished without fatal errors; false otherwise.

demultiplexed_reads.reasoning: This node is a Signal, so I included only technical properties of the per-sample read file artefacts: file format, file size, read count, read length, and file-level quality status. I excluded demultiplexing software and parameters because those belong to the upstream Process node, and I excluded any biological or processed-abundance interpretation because that belongs downstream. The goal is to describe the per-sample sequencing files as stored after run processing so users can verify completeness and technical suitability for denoising.

md_schema.descr: Technical file format used for the per-sample sequencing reads after demultiplexing, typically FASTQ or a compressed FASTQ variant. Record the format of the read artefact as stored after processing.

Total size of the demultiplexed read file or file bundle, measured in bytes at the time of storage or transfer. This supports integrity checks and storage tracking for the processed sequencing signal artifact.
Number of sequencing reads contained in the per-sample demultiplexed file, counted after basecalling and sample assignment. This value is used to assess sample yield before denoising.

Nominal read length in base pairs for the demultiplexed read file, recorded as the per-read length represented in the artifact. For paired-end data, this should match the retained read length after processing.

Technical quality flag associated with the demultiplexed read file, indicating whether the per-sample artifact was accepted, flagged, or rejected during ingestion. Use this to represent file-level integrity rather than biological quality.

denoising_process.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I included only algorithmic and parameter settings for denoising the sequencing reads into ASVs, plus a process outcome indicator. I excluded the input demultiplexed read file properties because those belong to the upstream Signal node, and I excluded the ASV table itself because that is the downstream Derivative node. Per the rules, the process node should capture the software package/version, key filtering parameters, and merge/truncation settings that define how reads were transformed. I kept the schema aligned with a DADA2-style denoising workflow used in 18S amplicon analysis.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software package or pipeline used to quality filter, error-correct, and merge reads into amplicon sequence variants. Record the exact processing tool used for this step.
Version of the denoising software used for read processing, recorded as a version string such as 'v1.30' or a semantic version. This is required for reproducibility of ASV inference.
Forward-read truncation length applied before denoising, measured in base pairs. This parameter determines how many bases were retained from the forward read during quality filtering.
Reverse-read truncation length applied before denoising, measured in base pairs. This parameter determines how many bases were retained from the reverse read during quality filtering.
Maximum expected errors threshold used to filter reads during denoising, recorded as a numeric cutoff. This controls the stringency of quality filtering before ASV inference.
Method used to identify and remove chimeric reads during denoising. Record the controlled category that best matches the algorithm applied in this step.
Indicator that the denoising process completed successfully and produced an ASV-ready result. Record true when the algorithm ran without fatal errors and yielded valid ASV calls; false otherwise.

asv_table.reasoning: This node is a Derivative, so I included only computed-result properties of the ASV abundance table itself: how it was generated, the table dimensions, sparsity/completeness indicators, and file/storage metadata. I excluded the denoising software and parameters because those belong to the upstream Process node, and I excluded taxonomy assignments because those belong to the downstream taxonomy derivative. The field set is meant to describe the derived abundance matrix as a reusable analytical product rather than the raw reads or the upstream sequencing settings.

md_schema.descr: Computational method used to generate the ASV abundance table from denoised reads, typically the denoising and inference approach applied upstream. Record the method name used for the derived abundance matrix.
Total number of unique amplicon sequence variants represented in the table, counted across all samples after denoising and filtering. This is a key dimension of the derived abundance matrix.
Number of freshwater samples represented as columns or rows in the ASV table, counted at the time the derivative was created. This reflects the table’s coverage across the study design.

Fraction of zero cells in the ASV abundance matrix, computed as the proportion of sample-ASV combinations with zero counts. Typical values in amplicon surveys are often high due to sparse community structure.
Indicator of whether the ASV table is stored as raw counts or normalized values. Use a controlled category to represent the analytical state of the derived table.
File format used to store the ASV abundance table derivative, such as TSV, CSV, BIOM, or another analytical container. This describes the technical packaging of the derived matrix.
Size of the ASV table file or file bundle, measured in bytes at the time of storage or export. This helps track the technical scale and completeness of the derived artifact.

taxonomy_assignment.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I included only the classification workflow details used to assign taxonomy to ASVs: the reference database, software, version, confidence thresholds, and process success. I excluded the ASV table itself because that is the upstream input, and I excluded the resulting taxonomy labels because those belong to the downstream taxonomy derivative node. I also avoided duplicating sequencing or denoising parameters already covered elsewhere. The schema is limited to reproducible taxonomic-assignment settings so users can understand how the classifications were produced.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software or pipeline used to assign taxonomy to the ASVs. Record the exact tool used for this classification step.

Version of the taxonomy assignment software used for the classification step, recorded as a version string such as 'v2024.5' or a semantic version. This is required for reproducibility of taxonomic calls.
Name of the reference database used to classify ASVs into eukaryotic taxonomy, such as SILVA, PR2, or another curated marker-gene database. Record the database employed for this assignment run.
Version or release identifier of the reference database used for taxonomy assignment. Use a version string or release date to identify the exact taxonomic reference set.

Minimum confidence or bootstrap threshold required to accept a taxonomic assignment, recorded as the cutoff used by the classifier. Typical values depend on the method and should be reported at the time of the assignment run.
Deepest taxonomic rank targeted or reported by the assignment workflow, recorded as a controlled category. This indicates the classification resolution used in the process.
Indicator that the taxonomy assignment process completed successfully and produced usable taxonomic classifications. Record true when classification ran without fatal errors; false otherwise.

taxonomy_table.reasoning: This node is a Derivative, so I included only computed taxonomy-result properties of the ASV annotations themselves: the taxonomy labels stored in the table, the number of ASVs classified, confidence/completeness indicators, and file/storage metadata. I excluded the classifier software, reference database, and thresholds because those belong to the upstream taxonomy assignment process. I also excluded sample metadata and raw abundance properties because those are on other nodes. The schema is intended to describe the taxonomy table as a derived annotation product that can be reused for ecological interpretation.

md_schema.descr: Computational method or classifier family used to generate the taxonomy table from ASVs, recorded as the derived annotation approach. This identifies how the taxonomic labels were produced.
Number of ASVs in the study that received a taxonomic annotation in the table, counted at the time the derivative was created. This indicates the extent of classification coverage.

Fraction of ASVs or taxonomic entries in the table that received an assignment to the target rank, computed as a completeness metric for the derivative. Values near 1 indicate broad classification coverage.

Summary statistic or categorical description of the confidence associated with the taxonomic labels in the table, capturing the overall reliability of the derived annotations. Record the project’s standardized summary if available.
File format used to store the taxonomy table derivative, such as TSV, CSV, JSON, or another tabular annotation format. This describes the technical packaging of the derived labels.
Size of the taxonomy table file or file bundle, measured in bytes at the time of storage or export. This helps track the technical scale and completeness of the derived artifact.

metadata_table_creation.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I included only the curation and table-building parameters for consolidating sample information and environmental measurements into the metadata table. I excluded the individual sample identity fields and the environmental signal values themselves because those belong to the upstream Entity and Signal nodes, and I excluded the final table contents because those belong to the downstream derivative. The process fields focus on software/workflow, column schema decisions, validation/curation status, and whether the table creation step succeeded. I avoided duplicating fields already generated for sample identity, measurement signals, and downstream analytical joins.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software, workflow, or script used to consolidate sample information and environmental measurements into the curated metadata table. Record the tool used for this curation step, such as a spreadsheet workflow, R script, or data pipeline.
Version of the software or pipeline used for metadata table creation, recorded as a version string when applicable. This supports reproducibility of the curation workflow.

Version identifier of the metadata column schema applied during table creation, describing the curated set of fields included in the final table. Use a project-specific version or release label such as 'v1.0' or '2024-06'.

Indicator of whether standardized curation rules, such as unit harmonization, controlled vocabulary mapping, or missing-value handling, were applied during table creation. Use a controlled category to summarize the curation approach used for the table.

Indicator that the assembled metadata table passed validation checks such as required-column presence, duplicate-sample detection, and unit consistency review. Record true when the table met project quality criteria; false otherwise.
Number of sample rows included in the curated metadata table at the time of creation, counted after consolidation and validation. This reflects the table’s coverage of the study samples.
Indicator that the metadata table creation process completed successfully and produced a usable curated table. Record true when the process finished without fatal errors; false otherwise.

sample_metadata_table.reasoning: This node is a Derivative, so I included only properties of the curated sample metadata table itself: its schema/coverage, completeness, storage format, and simple quality indicators. I excluded the underlying lake, depth, zone, season, and environmental values because those are the table contents rather than metadata about the table as an artifact. I also excluded the creation workflow details because those belong to the upstream metadata_table_creation process. The goal is to describe the final curated metadata table as a reusable dataset product, not to repeat the sample-level measurements it contains.

md_schema.descr: Version identifier of the curated sample metadata schema represented in the table, describing the final set of sample and environmental columns included. Use a project-specific version or release label such as 'v1.0' or '2024-06'.
Number of sample rows contained in the metadata table at the time it was finalized, counted after curation and validation. This indicates how many freshwater samples are represented.
Number of columns included in the curated sample metadata table, counted at the time the derivative was created. This reflects the breadth of sample descriptors and environmental variables stored.

Fraction of required sample metadata fields populated across the table, computed as the proportion of non-missing values for mandatory columns. Typical values range from 0 to 1 and summarize curation completeness.
File format used to store the curated metadata table, such as CSV, TSV, Excel, JSON, or another tabular container. This describes the technical packaging of the derived table.
Overall quality flag for the curated metadata table, indicating whether the table is ready for downstream integration and analysis. Use a controlled category to summarize the derivative’s usability.
Size of the metadata table file or file bundle, measured in bytes at the time of storage or export. This helps track the technical scale and completeness of the derived artifact.

community_environment_join.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I included only the join/integration workflow settings used to combine the ASV abundance table with the curated sample metadata table. I excluded the upstream ASV and metadata table contents because those belong to the input derivatives, and I excluded the integrated output dataset itself because that belongs to the downstream derivative node. The fields focus on the software used for the merge, join keys, merge behavior, record retention rules, and whether the integration succeeded, which are the minimum reproducibility details for the integration step.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software, library, or workflow used to join the ASV abundance data with sample metadata. Record the exact tool used for this integration step, such as an R data manipulation package or pipeline.
Version of the software or package used to perform the community-environment join, recorded as a version string when applicable. This supports reproducibility of the integration workflow.
Field names used to link the ASV abundance table to the sample metadata table during the join, such as sample identifier columns. Record the exact join keys as used in the integration step.

Join strategy used to combine the ASV and sample metadata tables, recorded as a controlled category describing record-retention behavior. Use the join type that matches the integration logic applied in the workflow.
Rule used to handle duplicate keys or repeated sample records during the integration step, recorded as a controlled category. This documents how the workflow resolved non-unique records.
Number of rows produced by the join operation, counted in the integrated table at the completion of the process. This reflects the size of the combined dataset before downstream analysis.
Indicator that the community-environment join completed successfully and produced a usable integrated table. Record true when the merge finished without fatal errors; false otherwise.

integrated_ecology_dataset.reasoning: This node is a Derivative, so I included only properties of the integrated analytical dataset itself: what inputs it combines, its dimensions, completeness, storage format, and a simple usability flag. I excluded the join software and merge logic because those belong to the upstream integration process, and I excluded the underlying ASV and environmental values because those are the contents of the dataset rather than metadata about the dataset artifact. The field set is intended to describe the final reusable analysis-ready product for freshwater microbial ecology.

md_schema.descr: Components combined in the integrated ecology dataset, describing the analytical content of the derivative. Record that the dataset includes 18S community composition and environmental metadata as the joined inputs.

Number of rows contained in the integrated ecology dataset at the time it was finalized, counted after joining community and environmental records. This indicates the size of the analysis-ready table.

Number of columns included in the integrated ecology dataset, counted at the time the derivative was created. This reflects the combined breadth of community and environmental variables available for analysis.

Fraction of expected integrated fields populated across the dataset, computed as the proportion of non-missing values for required columns. Typical values range from 0 to 1 and summarize analytical completeness.

File or storage format used for the integrated ecology dataset, such as CSV, TSV, RDS, parquet, or another tabular analytical container. This describes the technical packaging of the derivative artifact.

Indicator that the integrated ecology dataset passed checks for downstream ecological analysis, such as successful row matching and required-field completeness. Record true when the dataset is ready for statistical analysis; false otherwise.
Size of the integrated ecology dataset file or file bundle, measured in bytes at the time of storage or export. This helps track the technical scale and completeness of the final derived artifact.
